Key Research Thinking Patterns: Geometry–Algebra Bridge: Establishes deep connections between geometric invariants (diameter, focal radius, leaf-space geometry) and algebraic structures (Veronese embeddings, Hilbert series, Cohen–Macaulay modules).

Symmetry-Driven Reduction: Systematically exploit group actions, polar representations, and fat sections to reduce high-dimensional or complex structures to tractable invariant subspaces and sections.
Rigidity and Classification: Characterizes equality cases in geometric inequalities via rigidity arguments and complete classifications (e.g., equality in extrinsic diameter vs focal radius).
Constructive Invariant Theory: Develops Laplacian algebras and generalized polarizations as concrete tools for generating invariants and understanding inverse invariant theory.
Generalization and Abstraction: Extends classical results (Kostant convexity, Lax conjecture, etc.) to broader contexts such as submetries, infinitesimal foliations, and nonpolar actions.
Interdisciplinary Synthesis: Combines differential geometry, spectral theory, convex geometry, and algebraic invariant theory to yield unified frameworks and transfer results across domains.

Summary Description: Ricardo A. E. Mendes is a mathematical theorist whose research spans differential geometry, geometric analysis, spectral geometry, and invariant theory. His work develops deep connections between geometric phenomena (submanifolds, focal geometry, leaf spaces of foliations, and submetries) and algebraic structures (Veronese embeddings, Hilbert series, Laplacian algebras, generalized polarizations). Mendes has contributed foundational results that unify Kostant’s convexity with modern metric geometry, establish Weyl-type laws for basic spectra in singular Riemannian foliations, and advance inverse invariant theory through the maximality of Laplacian algebras. His research routinely leverages symmetry to reduce complex problems, derives complete classifications of equality cases, and provides constructive frameworks for generating invariants and reducing optimization problems under symmetry (spectrahedra and their shadows). Across collaborations with researchers such as Marco Radeschi, Renato Bettiol, Mario Kummer, and Samuel Lin, Mendes’ work exemplifies a coherent program that blends geometric insights with algebraic and computational perspectives to address foundational questions at the intersection of geometry, algebra, and optimization.
Open Questions & Future Directions: Existence and scope of Weyl-type asymptotics for the basic spectrum without assuming basic mean curvature in singular Riemannian foliations (extensions beyond Theorem A).
Weyl-type results for foliations with nonclosed leaves and the corresponding leaf-space volume invariants.
Refinements of Hilbert-series expansions and higher-term coefficients in relation to pole structure and geometric data in the SRF context.

Relaxing k-NS (k-normal spaces condition) in generalized polarization frameworks and identifying minimal sufficient conditions for generation of invariant algebras via generalized polarizations (Theorem F, G in related work).
Exploration of broader fat-section/submetry settings to further generalize Kostant’s convexity and determine when quotient-convexity corresponds to convex lifts in higher generality.
